revised._assert_counts_realized_not_drawn: the three-base replacement draw. A substitution drew its replacement from all four bases including the one already at the site, so about a quarter of draws wrote back what was there; such a write changes nothing and was correctly not counted, which left `mutate(model="uniform")`, `pcr_amplify` and `sequencing_errors` delivering ~76% of their configured count. The draw now excludes the base at the site, so realized equals requested. This helper's third assertion was `sum(changed) < draws`, with its own comment saying why: the shortfall was what told a realized count apart from a drawn one on this fixture. The shortfall is gone, so the assertion is inverted to `sum(changed) == draws` -- not weakened but repointed, and it now fails if the four-base draw ever returns. The per-record equality above it, which is the load-bearing claim and compares the counter against a cross-run count of changed positions, is untouched. What the inversion does cost is the evidence that the counter is not simply the drawn count; that is replaced by a new Rust test, `pcr_error_count_is_what_was_applied_not_what_was_drawn`, covering the one configuration where the two still differ -- a permissive contract that admits no replacement anywhere leaves a requested error undelivered.

revised.test_pin_present_authored_p_plane_produc: The gate was 'at least 10 of 50 records per end', which is the mean of the weakest authored rate (J_5 at 0.2) and therefore failed about half the time by construction. Now 1000 records against the authored probability with a 0.05 tolerance, over three standard deviations at every rate -- and a stronger claim, because a two-sided band also catches a plane that reaches the engine too strongly.
revised.test_indel_insertion_creates_gap_in_germ: Asserted four gaps for four insertions. The germline alignment writes the NP regions as N padding, so a base inserted between two segments extends that padding rather than opening a gap -- which is what one of the four insertions now does. The gap count is asserted against the per-segment indel counters instead, which is exact rather than approximate, with n_indels == 4 and no gap in the sequence alignment kept as before.
revised.test_no_genotype_preserves_sampling_whil: The digest moved because the sampling model moved, which is what a determinism-version bump means. Recaptured at DETERMINISM_VERSION 2, with the module docstring now saying what this digest can and cannot be asked -- it answers 'did the genotype machinery disturb an unconstrained run', not 'does this version agree with an older one' -- and the assertion message telling the next reader which of the two cases they are in.
revised.test_end_to_end_planed_novel_flows_to_re: 50 records became 400, and the assertion gained a premise. The novel can only be called on a record that draws its gene, and the reference carries 52 V genes, so 50 records miss the gene outright about 38% of the time: the assertion was a coin flip that happened to land until the draw order moved. It now asserts that the gene was drawn at all, separately from the novel being reachable on it, so a failure says which of the two went wrong.
revised.test_run_cohort_mixed_novel_and_plain_su: 40 records per subject became 400, for the same reason as test_end_to_end_planed_novel_flows_to_records -- at 40 the gene is missed about 46% of the time. The claim is also sharpened: subject A is homozygous for the novel, so EVERY record of A's that draws the gene must call it, where 'at least one record calls it' was a weaker shadow. Subject B's half is unchanged.
revised.UNCLAIMED_FIELDS: Gains `determinism_version`, the new per-record stamp naming which sampling model drew the row. No mechanism can own it: it is the same number on every record the installed engine produces, and it is answerable to the reproducibility claim rather than to any biology.
revised.test_the_documented_conditions_for_produ: The bucket of records that satisfy the four documented conditions and are unproductive anyway is now partitioned by the engine's reason, because two different things put a record there. The tail-frame rule -- the documentation defect this test measures -- keeps the >= threshold unchanged. The other is the ORACLE being wrong: when a trim or deletion takes the germline anchor away, the engine says so and still exports a junction window with a fallback end, and `anchors_intact` reads the last codon of that window, which can translate to W or F by coincidence. Pre-existing and not about indels -- 4 of 600 indel-free human_igh records are anchor-removed with a junction exported, one with j_trim_5=15 -- and what per-pass substreams changed is only that one IGK record now lands in both buckets at once. That bucket is bounded at 2 so it cannot grow quietly, every record in it must carry a trim or indel that could remove an anchor, and anything in neither bucket now fails. Strictly more is asserted than before.
revised.anchors_intact: Docstring only, recording the blind spot the test above measures: it cannot tell a surviving anchor from a fallback junction window whose last codon reads W or F by coincidence. Answering that needs the reference anchor offset against the trims, which the record does not carry.
revised.test_all_failed_attempts_recorded_and_fo: the premise was the literal seed 0 under a comment calling the seed "a scheduling label". It is a label, which is why it cannot carry the premise: it says nothing about whether the family drawn under it survived. A clonal family's growth now draws from a named substream instead of the run seed directly, so seed 0's first attempt lives and there is no retry to record -- the test was asserting len(attempts) > 1 against a list of one. It now searches for a seed whose founder actually went extinct before a later attempt survived (two thirds of attempts do at lambda_base=0.4, so the search ends almost immediately), and every assertion that follows is unchanged and runs against the retried capture it asked for. The search runs on its own compiled experiment so it cannot disturb the proxy that counts founder draws.
revised.test_actual_execution_policy_and_prepare: the embedded source trace's schema version was asserted as the literal 4 and the engine now emits 5, because a trace file records which sampling model drew it. The claim here is that a receipt embeds a source trace at all, not which version it is at, so the assertion compares against `TraceFile.SCHEMA_VERSION`. Nothing else in the test changed and no assertion was weakened: a receipt embedding a stale version still fails.

test_the_reason_counts_one_unresolved_an.why: the pin recorded the limitation this branch removes. It asserted that reference_anchor_unresolved appears once per unresolved anchor and stated, in its docstring, that the record does NOT say which anchor -- the count was information and the attribution was missing. The successor asserts the attribution: the set of segments the reasons name equals the set whose allele is unresolved, and the unqualified spelling is gone from the vocabulary. Same records, same 200-record draw, strictly more pinned.

test_the_pass_with_no_counter_of_its_own.why: the predecessor asserted that ambiguous_base_calls moves no counter at all, because assay.ambiguous_calls declared a truth gap: the masking count lived in the trace as corrupt.ns.count and nowhere in the record. Its own failure message instructed this change -- 'assay.ambiguous_calls no longer declares a truth gap, so its count may now be exported -- in which case this test should check it moves'. n_ambiguous_bases is now exported, so the successor asserts the positive: exactly n_ambiguous_bases moves and no other owned counter, and its value equals the number of positions that actually differ from the unmasked run on the same seed. Strictly more pinned -- the predecessor could not distinguish a correct zero from a counter that had stopped reporting.

split_by_case.why: same partition, honest substrate. The predecessor split an untemplated run into its P and N parts by letter case, which is the convention at the moment the recombination writes a base and not afterwards: sequencing_errors lowercases what it corrupts and hypermutation writes uppercase, so case stops naming the origin as soon as either runs. The successor reads the engine's p_nucleotide_mask. It takes the simulation as a parameter because the answer lives there rather than in the run's bytes, and it is renamed because a function called split_by_case that no longer splits by case is a trap for the next reader. Nothing outside this module's own REPORTS registry called it.

test_pcr_substitution_base_distribution_.why: the three-base replacement draw. A substitution drew its replacement from all four bases including the one already at the site, so about a quarter of draws wrote back what was there; such a write changes nothing and was correctly not counted, which left `mutate(model="uniform")`, `pcr_amplify` and `sequencing_errors` delivering ~76% of their configured count. The draw now excludes the base at the site, so realized equals requested. This predecessor asserted the MARGINAL over A/C/G/T is uniform at 0.25 each, which cannot hold once the draw is conditional, and not because of a defect: on its own fixture `A` occupies 6 of the 15 templated positions, so `A` is the base most often excluded and its marginal falls to a measured 0.2096. The successor asserts the conditional claim the model actually makes -- given the base at the site, the replacement is uniform over the other three and never that base -- from a transition table built by pairing each error's recorded site with its recorded base, restricted to single-error records at a position the fixture fixes. Measured 1,276 samples, four rows of 482/265/284/245, diagonal empty. Strictly stronger: the marginal test would have passed a draw that sometimes wrote the incumbent and spread the remainder evenly.

test_full_stack_replay_reproduces_commit.why: the committed golden it compared against is the compat suite's frozen anchor, and regenerating it was the wrong way to settle a deliberate model change. The predecessor compared a live run at seed 4242 against `tests/golden/trace_files/full_stack_seed4242.trace.json`, so it fails whenever a sampling model changes on purpose -- the three-base replacement draw did exactly that, moving `corrupt.pcr.error_base[0]`. Regenerating the file would have destroyed what `test_v1_fixtures_exist_in_committed_set` and `test_v1_fixture_has_no_v2_fields_serialised` exist to protect: a fixture written by an older build, which is the only way to prove v1 -> current compatibility at the next schema bump. The successor keeps every assertion the predecessor made about the replay -- the migrated-prefix check, the signature comparison, the length and per-choice address+value equality under the drained cursor -- and takes them against a file it writes to a temporary directory itself, so there is no committed artifact to go stale. It also adds `assert a_choices`, which the predecessor lacked: an empty trace satisfied every comparison in it. Durability of the frozen artifacts stays with `test_trace_file_compat.py`, which already loads them, parses every address and replays them record for record; cross-platform determinism of the values stays with `tests/acceptance/test_reproducibility.py`.

test_an_off_pass_keeps_the_rearrangement.why: The old test asserted that an off pass DOES shift the draws behind it -- `same_sequence == 0` over 40 records -- because the engine held one random stream for the whole plan. Its own docstring said that if per-pass substreams were ever added the sequence half would start passing and the test should be replaced by the stronger claim. They were. The successor asserts the opposite and more: every exported field identical, molecule included, on every record. Renamed because the old name states the old behaviour.

test_the_one_pass_whose_off_switch_is_no.why: It pinned `invert_d(prob=0.0)` re-drawing NP2 at exactly the precision of that finding, and said in its own docstring that if the finding were ever fixed the test and the declaration should both be deleted. Fixed: with its own substream the pass moves nothing at prob=0.0, measured over 200 records. The claim is now covered, unconditionally and for every pass with an off switch, by the parametrized test named above -- which previously had a branch that exempted this one.

test_duplex_recoverable_count_ignores_li.why: The old test asserted that adding a PCR pass leaves `n_observable_mutations` identical. That is not true and cannot be: a misincorporation landing on a mutated base draws a base the site does not hold, which includes the germline base one time in three, and writing the germline base back erases the evidence that the mutation happened -- which is what 'observable' means. One of six records now loses one. It was invisible while the PCR pass's presence shifted the mutation pass's draws, because the two runs were different molecules and no position could be compared; per-pass substreams make them the same molecule plus the errors. The successor asserts what the claim really is: `n_mutations` identical, the recoverable count never rising, and every drop accounted for by a position the clean run mutated and the noisy run restored. Renamed because the old name states the false claim.

test_emit_golden_trace_file_for_future_b.why: It compared a fresh run against the committed v1 trace fixture and said a failure meant either a schema bump or a determinism regression. A third case arrived: a deliberate determinism change, which moves every recorded value. Regenerating the fixture was not available -- it is the canonical v1 backwards-compat anchor that test_trace_file_compat.py::test_v1_fixtures_exist_in_committed_set exists to keep, and overwriting it would destroy the only proof that a v1 file still loads. So the two claims are separated, the same way the full-stack replay test was in this branch: durability of the on-disk format against old files stays with test_trace_file_compat.py over the frozen fixtures, and what remains here is a round trip through a file the test writes itself, which cannot go stale.

test_fresh_emission_carries_schema_versi.why: the trace-file schema is now version 5 (a trace file now records which sampling model drew it). This test asserted the literal 4, which is not what it is about: naming a version in a test is how a test about behaviour becomes a test about an integer -- it fails on every bump, the failure says nothing, and the fix is to retype the number. One of the two had already drifted, carrying a docstring about v3 under an assertion of 4. Both now compare against `TraceFile.SCHEMA_VERSION`, which is unconditionally true and still catches an emission that writes a stale version; every other assertion in each test is unchanged.

test_v4_records_policy_and_actual_contra.why: the trace-file schema is now version 5 (a trace file now records which sampling model drew it). This test asserted the literal 4, which is not what it is about: naming a version in a test is how a test about behaviour becomes a test about an integer -- it fails on every bump, the failure says nothing, and the fix is to retype the number. One of the two had already drifted, carrying a docstring about v3 under an assertion of 4. Both now compare against `TraceFile.SCHEMA_VERSION`, which is unconditionally true and still catches an emission that writes a stale version; every other assertion in each test is unchanged. The successor also keeps the >= 4 floor, since the two fields it checks were introduced at v4 and are a guarantee from v4 onward.

The one test that read the constant no longer reads a committed artifact -- see replaced['test_full_stack_replay_reproduces_committed_golden_trace'] -- so the constant named a file this module no longer touches.
